name: umka-lang
why: A statically typed embeddable scripting language with a small, unusual design that is fun to try in a short sitting.

brief.what_it_is: Umka is a statically typed scripting language that can be embedded in other programs. It has Go-like syntax with compile-time type checking, and ships as a bytecode compiler and virtual machine. The README describes it as a scripting language with a lightweight interpreter that can be embedded into an application as a shared library. The CLI executable is umka, and the language is written in C99.
brief.why_it_exists: The README contrasts Umka with Go: Go is a compiled systems language with a complex runtime and big output binaries, while Umka aims to be a small scripting language with a lightweight interpreter that is easy to embed. Its guiding principle is Explicit is better than implicit.
brief.how_it_works: Source is compiled to bytecode and run on a virtual machine, with garbage collection. The README says it is distributed as a static or dynamic library with a simple C API, so a host C program can load and call into Umka code. Multitasking uses fibers (lightweight threads) rather than goroutines and channels.
brief.install_notes: Install with Homebrew (formula umka-lang), or download a stable release from the GitHub releases page; the README says releases are for Windows and Linux. An unstable build is available as a box.tar from UmBox, and UmBox also hosts packages. The README does not show a shell command for running a .um file. Running the C+Umka 3D example requires raylib. Otherwise the README mentions no accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration. The playground at vtereshkov.github.io/umka-lang runs it in a browser with no install.
brief.standout: Unusual design choices: Pascal-style p^ for dereference instead of *p, with * repurposed as the export mark as in Oberon; a :-separated declaration syntax; explicit capture lists for closures; and a ternary operator that Go omits. It also has no separate slice type, using dynamic arrays instead, and fibers in place of goroutines. The README includes a 400 x 400 matrix multiply benchmark and a set of real projects built with it, including games, a finite element demo and a text editor port.
brief.status: Maintained. The releases page lists Umka 1.5.7 as Latest, dated 22 Aug (the year is not shown in the scraped page). Umka 1.5.6 is dated 06 Apr, and the 1.5.x line has a steady series of releases. The README has a CI badge and an active Discord.
brief.caveats: The README lists stable downloads only for Windows and Linux; macOS is not mentioned there, though Homebrew is offered. The performance chart is from older hardware (AMD A4-3300M, Windows 7). The raylib dependency applies to the 3D example. The README does not state a licence, and I did not follow the docs links, so details of the language and stdlib are not verified. The README shows no quick-start command, so readers may need the docs to run their first script.
quotes: Umka is a statically typed embeddable scripting language. It combines simplicity and flexibility with compile-time type checking, following the principle Explicit is better than implicit.
It doesn't have slices as separate data types. Instead, it supports dynamic arrays, which are declared like Go's slices and initialized by calling make().
